headline: South Asia: Flights resume at Riyadh airport after two-week closure as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Flights resume at Riyadh airport after two-week closure as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia.
- India: Trump Says "Gotta Stop" Killing Iran Leaders To Know Who US Is Dealing With.
- Western Russia: Four killed and 14 injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast – video.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Morgan wants criminal sanctions for defamation.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Morgan wants criminal sanctions for defamation.
Government senator Marlon Morgan has called for the reintroduction of criminal sanctions for defamation in Jamaica. Making his contribution to the State of the Nation Debate in the Upper House on Friday, Morgan took aim at the parliamentary Opposition and those he referred to as their surrogates and supporters on social media, blasting them for tarnishing people’s reputation. He warned that the misinformation and disinformation being peddled by these persons serve to undermine the country’s democracy.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: PATHWAYS MURDER TRIAL | Second JP backs claim Ruddock was not forced to give statement.
A second justice of the peace (JP) on Friday testified that Andre Ruddock voluntarily gave police a statement in which he allegedly confessed to cutting Taneka Gardner’s throat. The witness corroborated earlier testimony from a colleague that Ruddock was not forced, threatened or harmed, nor offered any inducement to give the caution statement, on October 18, 2021 – a day after Gardner was killed in an alleged sacrificial ritual at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St James.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: What to know about AI-detected Internet security bug.
AP: The language that’s known as the backbone of the Internet is now subject to what experts describe as one of the most notable vulnerabilities in recent memory. PHP is a widely used general-purpose scripting language that is geared toward web development, and thus, it powers the majority of websites around the world. When the organisation behind the language and the Federal Bureau of Investigations’ cyber division warned Wednesday of significant vulnerabilities in the language, government agencies, corporations and other organisations were sent into a flurry.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Four killed and 14 injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast – video.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 15 hours ago: Four killed and 14 injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast – video.
Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast killed four people and injured 14, including an 11-year-old girl.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 14 hours ago: Three firefighters injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv – photo.
Russian forces attacked Kharkiv with drones on the evening of 24 October. Four people, including three firefighters, were injured in the strikes.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: One killed and five injured in Russian drone strike on bus in Kherson – photos.
Kherson City Military Administration has reported six civilian casualties after a Russian drone hit a passenger-filled bus on the afternoon of 25 October.
- The Moscow Times, 6 hours ago: Ukrainian Attacks Kill 5 in Belgorod and Lipetsk, Hit Perm Industrial Plant.
Four people were killed in southwestern Russia’s Belgorod region and one in the Lipetsk region.
Southern Europe: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Trump rules out Sunday strike on Iran as Netanyahu warns Israel faces imminent existential threat.
- Jerusalem Post, South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: Trump rules out Sunday strike on Iran as Netanyahu warns Israel faces imminent existential threat.
Trump also said that the US is actively monitoring activity at Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site as well as three other sites that were allegedly destroyed in previous strikes.
- Jerusalem Post, 4 hours ago: IDF seriously injures, fails to detain Palestinian accused of attempted ramming attack - report.
According to Army Radio, the incident occured on Friday near Kafr Dura, shortly after the fatal Hebron attack that killed Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem.
- Jerusalem Post, 6 hours ago: Ex-Mossad chief Barnea intended for Iran to see Israel's operations to overwhelm IRGC.
On June 13, 2025, the Mossad released sensational and rare video footage of its co-lead role with the air force in Israel's preemptive strike on Iran's ballistic missiles and air defenses.
- Jerusalem Post, NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Netanyahu shares AI-generated image of nuclear explosion in Tel Aviv, two days before election.
The prime minister's Instagram post, warning of Iran's nuclear threat, drew criticism from opposition leaders Yair Golan and Gadi Eisenkot, who accused him of using fear as an election tactic.
Africa - bottom line: Iranian president blames United States for failure of interim peace deal.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Iranian president blames United States for failure of interim peace deal.
Masoud Pezeshkian emphasised, however, that a new attempt should be made to reach an agreement to end the war with the US and Israel.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Flights resume at Riyadh airport after two-week closure as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Africanews, The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: Flights resume at Riyadh airport after two-week closure as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia.
Flights resumed at Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday following a series of deadly attacks on the facility that saw it closed for two weeks, even as Yemen’s Houthi rebels targeted the country with strikes. King Khalid International Airport’s website showed several domestic and international flights scheduled on Sunday, including arrivals to the kingdom from Dubai, Paris and Cairo. The renewed operations at the airport came as explosions rattled Riyadh early Sunday, after a text message was sent to residents warning of a hostile threat targeting the city.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: The nuclear danger at sea.
Dawn’s October 23 editorial rightly warned about India’s nuclear-armed submarine patrols. The danger is larger than a new vessel at sea. It is a sea-based nuclear force growing alongside precision-strike capabilities, missile defence and a false confidence in initiating military action. Imagining that these developments confer a first-strike advantage or create a safe space for war is imprudent. Pakistan has the capability and resolve to preserve the strategic balance.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Israeli strike on Gaza university kills 3; another 4 Palestinians killed in other attacks.
An Israeli strike on a university in Gaza City killed three people on Sunday, staff and a local hospital said, while the civil defence agency reported four others killed elsewhere in the territory. Reached for comment, the Israeli military said it was looking into the reports. Al Shifa Hospital said it received three bodies and treated eight people who were wounded in the Gaza City drone strike, with two sources at the Islamic University saying those killed were administrative staff and the injured were students.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: How Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump.
Relations between United States President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky took a sharp downward turn in recent weeks, with each leader openly criticising the other. The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump’s frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv’s supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward.
India - bottom line: Trump Says "Gotta Stop" Killing Iran Leaders To Know Who US Is Dealing With.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Trump Says "Gotta Stop" Killing Iran Leaders To Know Who US Is Dealing With.
In the first few weeks of the war, the US and Israel killed several of Iran's top political and military leaders, including Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in airstrikes.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Ukraine hits back at Musk’s claim over civilian Starlink use for offensive strikes.
Ukraine's military firmly dismissed Elon Musk's claims that Starlink was used for offensive drone strikes. A Ukrainian defence technology adviser confirmed that limitations prevented such usage, countering Musk's assertions. Connectivity issues have further hampered military efforts amid ongoing Russian assaults, prompting renewed diplomatic engagement. Concurrently, Ukraine faces a surge in drone strikes on its urban centers.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: 'Wars Being Fought By Attacking Economies': PM Modi On "Cyber Terrorists".
Addressing a gathering after inaugurating the Reserve Bank of India's Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute here, he said the facilities would greatly benefit the people of Odisha and the country.
- Times of India - Top Stories, NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: BJP calls for nationwide protest over Kharge’s ‘baap’ remark.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's comment about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's father sparked widespread outrage among BJP members. Following the incident, the BJP announced nationwide protests against Kharge's remarks, labeling them indecent and offensive. Union home minister Amit Shah criticized Congress for personal attacks and blamed it on their electoral disappointments. Kharge also condemned the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, describing it as a threat to democracy.

- Taipei Times, just now: UK, French troops war-game attack on NATO.
- South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: Israel widens West Bank crackdown, displacing Hebron families after attack.
Israel said on Sunday all land crossings with the West Bank will be closed on the day of next week’s election, as it pledged a harder line on militancy after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers in the territory. - South China Morning Post - China, 18 hours ago: Gulf economies accelerate diversification as recession looms over Iran war.
Before the outbreak of the war triggered by the US-Israeli attack on Iran in February, the Gulf monarchies were living the prosperity dream that was the envy of the world. Their hydrocarbon-fuelled economies were glitzy oases of growth, inoculated from the conflict in Gaza that had rocked other parts of the Middle East for several years. Underpinned by decades-old US security guarantees and conflict mediation by billionaire sheikhs, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar cultivated...
- South China Morning Post - China, 10 hours ago: China’s Liaoning carrier and USS Theodore Roosevelt may be in Philippine Sea at same time.
China’s Liaoning aircraft carrier strike group sailed beyond the first island chain last week to reach the southernmost waters of the Philippines, suggesting an intent to position itself closer to ongoing US-Japan joint exercises. Philippine news channel BNC reported that the carrier group reached about 25 nautical miles (46km) east-southeast of Balut Island, the southernmost point of the Philippines, before sailing northeast on Friday. That positioned the warships past the first island chain, a...
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Kim Jong Un says North Korea ‘inspired’ by China’s success in border city visit.
- NK News, 22 hours ago: Kim Jong Un says North Korea ‘inspired’ by China’s success in border city visit.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said his country is “inspired” by China’s success during a visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday marking the 76th anniversary of China entering the Korean War, according to DPRK state media. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported Sunday on Kim’s visit to the “Memorial […]

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Remote community devastated over closure of Indigenous youth organisation.
- ABC News Australia, just now: Remote community devastated over closure of Indigenous youth organisation.
It has been a month since the Wyndham Aboriginal Youth Corporation in northern Western Australia closed its doors without warning. The organisation has been credited with reducing crime rates.
- The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Morning Mail: surge in bulk-billing by GPs; Deloitte under pressure over error-filled WA report; and anger over Neighbours’ AI recut.
Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here, and finish your day with our Politics, really newsletter. Good morning. We lead on new data revealing that almost two-thirds of Australians are now bulk-billed for all their GP care, after the government introduced financial incentives for doctors and practices. WA’s government wants its money back after a report by consultancy firm Deloitte was found to contain errors, including AI hallucinations and hundreds of millions of dollars in cost discrepancies.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Live: Wall Street retreats as oil prices continue to rise, ASX set to slip.
Oil prices have jumped, putting downward pressure on global stock markets, including the ASX. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: SA 'disproportionately vulnerable' to NDIS changes, report warns.
South Australia was once the launch site for children under 14 on the NDIS. Now it is grappling with how to handle the federal government’s sweeping changes to the scheme.
